title: Monitor system, rented instruments and the harp
summary: His brother built a monitor system; the truck overturned in Vermont.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: You must have had some fiendish problems especially getting on the road, balancing the woodwinds and all that.

My brother made a monitor system so that we could--he designed the thing and set it up for us. He built it because we had no money and he laid out the money and did it. We could not afford it otherwise. We didn't know how that was going to work either. He did it in such a way that it would just boost that high end, the harp and the celeste; I still have the
downstairs; the glockenspiel, and we didn't buy all this stuff, we rented it all from Carol with the intent to buy; that's what happened.
We had to get a truck to transport it and break in people to handle all this stuff and they didn't always do that well, especially with the sound equipment. They were a little rough with it.
That stuff couldn't take the beatings that it takes now.
One time the truck rolled over in Vermont and the harp went bouncing down a hill. It came to the job that night full of holes; fortunately nobody got hurt, but I'm glad it didn't happen more.
The road is a frightful thing.
